writeup.p: S18PacketEntityTeleport carries an absolute fixed-point position (ints x 32), rotation bytes and an onGround flag for one entity. It is the only entity-position packet with full coordinates, so it is both the correction mechanism for accumulated S14 error and the transport for genuine jumps: ender pearls, endermen, dimension changes and anything that moves more than 4 blocks in one tick. EntityTrackerEntry constructs it when the tracked entity's one-tick displacement exceeds the relative-move threshold (corpus line 222), and NetHandlerPlayServer sends it to a player on teleport (line 259).

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleEntityTeleport (Memeware 7.3 bundle, line 511) overwrites serverPosX/Y/Z with the absolute values, computes position as serverPos / 32.0 with y + 0.015625 (half a block in fixed point, the eye-height accommodation), decodes yaw/pitch as * 360 / 256, and calls setPositionAndRotation2 with interpolation 3 and the teleport flag. If the entity is already within 0.03125 blocks (x/z) and 0.015625 (y) of the target it keeps the current position and applies only rotation, which prevents micro-jitter on repeated teleports.

Five distinct consumers in the corpus. Rise 6.x: LegitReach snaps its realPosition to the absolute coordinates, WatchdogVelocity includes S18 in its spoof packet set and re-anchors on it, and PingSpoofComponent classifies it in the players tuple so teleports are delayed with the rest of the entity stream. Rise 5.99: PlayerData re-anchors serverPosX/Y/Z and zeroes ticksSinceLastTeleport so checks skip the teleport tick. Sigma 4.11: Ranking treats S18 as an entity-removal signal that finalizes kill/death records. Tenacity 6.0: AntiExploit cancels S18 with any coordinate beyond 30,000,000. Spicy: NoClip and Phase import the class but never branch on it, a leftover from their Sigma 2 lineage.

S18 is clientbound and absolute, so the abuse direction is server to client: a malicious server can emit fixed-point coordinates that corrupt client-side position bookkeeping or trigger bounds bugs, which is exactly what Tenacity's AntiExploit threshold mitigates. For cheats, S18 is the epoch boundary of every position-based state machine: accumulated S14 error resets here, so reach and backtrack modules must re-anchor their reconstructed positions on it. The S08PacketPlayerPosLook + S18 pair is the server's complete teleport vocabulary, and disablers and reach modules watch both because a missed teleport poisons every later delta.

overview: The absolute teleport packet is the reset point of entity position state. Cheat clients re-anchor their reconstructed position caches on it (LegitReach, WatchdogVelocity, Rise 5.99 anticheat), Sigma uses it as an entity-left signal, Tenacity hardens against server-side coordinate abuse, and Spicy's movement modules carry it as a dead import.
server_handling: The server side only emits S18, never validates it on receive. EntityTrackerEntry chooses it when the tracked entity moved 4+ blocks in a tick, and NetHandlerPlayServer sends it to a player being teleported. The client handler overwrites the entity's serverPosX/Y/Z, applies the +0.015625 y offset, keeps the current position when the entity is already within a 32nd of a block (rotation-only update), then interpolates with the teleport flag set. Because the client trusts the coordinates, a server can move an entity anywhere in the fixed-point range, which is the abuse AntiExploit guards against.
protocol_notes: Three ints (x 32), two bytes (x 256/360) and a boolean follow the VarInt entityId. The y offset of 0.015625 (0.5 / 32) is applied only on the client and is not part of the wire value. S18 supersedes any pending S14 deltas for the same entity because it overwrites the accumulated serverPosX/Y/Z. The packet is also sent to a player on respawn and dimension change, which is why Ranking's S08 + S18 combination distinguishes death from mere teleport.
anticheat_landscape: Server anticheats emit S18 as a correction and watch whether the client's later C03 positions rejoin the corrected location; a client that ignores the teleport or desyncs after it flags as position desync. The S08+S18 pair is the standard disabler/reach watch point: modules that delay clientbound traffic must flush on it or their position cache goes permanently stale. The client-side mirror (Rise 5.99 PlayerData) uses ticksSinceLastTeleport to suppress checks for a tick, an acknowledgment that even legitimate teleports produce movement anomalies.

modules.name: LegitReach
modules.purpose: Re-anchor the tracked target's server-truth position on the absolute teleport so the ping-spoof reach window keeps measuring the real distance.
modules.how_it_works: In the same PacketReceiveEvent handler that accumulates S14 deltas, an S18 for the tracked target replaces realPosition with new Vec3(getX() / 32D, getY() / 32D, getZ() / 32D). Without this branch, a teleported target would leave the accumulated position permanently wrong and the reach window would either never open or stay open against a ghost position.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Re-anchoring is a correctness requirement, not an exploit: a stale realPosition makes the module either inert or visibly wrong. The reach abuse itself lives in the ping-spoof half, not in the S18 handling.
modules.variations: Identical module in Rise 6.1.30 (path without the Client-release2 prefix).

modules.name: Ranking
modules.purpose: Track kills and deaths for the client's stats system; an S18 teleport for a tracked player finalizes the pending record because a teleporting opponent is out of reach context.
modules.how_it_works: A hidden, always-on module registered for EventAttack, EventPacket and EventUpdate. On EventAttack it records HitEntity entries per player; S0B animations timestamp attacker candidates; on S18 it calls onEntityRemoved(entityId), which flips the HitEntity to removed and reports killed() or prosecuted() if a chat message already matched the name in the last 3 seconds. S08PacketPlayerPosLook resets all prosecutor records (death/respawn), S13 destroys remove entities, S40 with 'ban' in the text reports a ban stat.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Passive telemetry collection; the S18 branch is just an entity-lifetime heuristic. No packet is mutated or replayed, so there is no detection surface.
modules.variations: The sendStat methods are stubs in the shipped source; the kill/death reporting path is a framework for a stats backend that was never filled in.

modules.name: NoClip / Phase
modules.purpose: Corpus hit is an import only: both movement modules import S18PacketEntityTeleport but never branch on it.
modules.how_it_works: NoClip's onEvent sends C03PacketPlayer.C04PacketPlayerPosition through sendPacketNoEvent when collided horizontally, then teleports the local player by 3 blocks up to break free; Phase cancels block hitboxes (EventGetBlockHitbox) and nudges the player position in a 3-stage loop while sending C03PacketPlayer(true). NoClip's header comment credits Sigma 2's Phase as the source, which explains the vestigial S18 import in both files.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The movement abuse is in the C03 stream, which is what anti-cheats flag (vertical motion while inside blocks). The unused S18 import has no effect on detection.
modules.variations: Phase.java (Spicy) carries the same dead import and additionally imports EventSendPacket; its hitbox-cancel approach is the more aggressive variant.

modules.name: AntiExploit
modules.purpose: Harden the client against server-side crash and grief exploits; the S18 branch blocks teleport coordinates beyond the world border.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketReceiveEvent, an S18 with any |getX()/getY()/getZ()| above 30,000,000 is cancelled and logged as 'Blocked Exploit: Teleport'. The same handler validates S48 resource pack URIs (http/https/level only, no path traversal), blocks S43 camera outside spectator, rejects particle floods, rate-limits S27 explosions and S11 experience orbs to 1 per millisecond, and caps total incoming packets at 100/second.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling clientbound packets is invisible to the server and cannot be flagged. The 30,000,000 bound matches the vanilla world border at which the server itself clamps movement.
modules.variations: Tenacity 6.0 is the only one of the 8 clients with a crash-exploit hardening module touching S18.

modules.name: WatchdogVelocity
modules.purpose: Include the teleport in the backtrack packet set and use it to re-anchor the tracked target's realPosition.
modules.how_it_works: isSpoof2Packet returns true for S18PacketEntityTeleport, so it is cancelled and queued with the S14 subclasses and S19 head look while the backtrack is active, and replayed through PacketUtil.receive on the flush conditions. Separately, an S18 for the target re-anchors realPosition to the absolute coordinates, keeping the distance gating (4.5/2.5 block thresholds) honest across teleports.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Holding a teleport client-side only delays the visual snap; the server state is unaffected. Flushing on hurtTime == 9 keeps the replay aligned with the player's damage timeline.
modules.variations: Not present in Rise 6.1.30's WatchdogVelocity corpus hit.

general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent across all consumers; the Rise 5.99 anticheat consumes S18 inside PlayerData.handle.
client_variations: Rise 6.x uses getX()/getY()/getZ() double accessors and divides by 32.0; Rise 5.99 and Sigma use the MCP-style func_149449_d/func_149451_c accessors; Tenacity reads getX() directly on the fixed-point ints (no /32), which is fine for the magnitude check. Only Rise 5.99 tracks ticksSinceLastTeleport as state.
